messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Group <leadership@redwood.com>; laura_bennett@redwood.com; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com; aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Draft OKR judgments + ask: evidence and one-line narratives for QBR

Team —

Attached is my draft scoring for Q4 OKRs (see Q4_OKR_scorecard.xlsx attached). I went through the objectives and assigned provisional judgments where we had measurable signals. Key notes:

- O1 (Inference unit cost): provisional 3/5. We hit a significant reduction on hosted but uneven on Dedicated cases. Need revenue-weighted clarification.
- O2 (Serving reliability): provisional 4/5 — infra SLOs met, but two P1 blips in Oct that impacted a small set of enterprise customers.
- O3 (Platform adoption): 2/5 — slower than target, pipeline conversion delayed by pricing negotiation cycles.

Ask list:
1) Please review the spreadsheet and add a one-line justification (1–2 sentences) per objective that I can paste into the QBR narrative.
2) Attach evidence links (runbooks, incident timelines, customer emails, HubSpot notes) for any objective where you disagree with the provisional score.
3) If you think a score should change, state the proposed score and a short evidence pointer.

Timeline: I need final edits and evidence by tomorrow, Tue 30 Nov 12:00pm PT — QBR deck build starts after that. If you cannot make the deadline, flag me now and I will coordinate follow-ups.

Attachments: Q4_OKR_scorecard.xlsx (WORKSHEET)

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft OKR judgments + ask: evidence and one-line narratives for QBR

Mina —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick disagreement on O1 (Inference unit cost). The hosted API numbers look right for the 18–20% improvement, but Dedicated shows a 25% drop in unit cost for committed pools once the reserved pricing kicked in. Aggregating those without weighting by revenue skews the judgment.

Proposal: split O1 into Hosted / Dedicated sub-lines on the narrative so the QBR reflects the nuance. I added comments in the spreadsheet (column: laura.comments) and linked a short cost-model snapshot in the Drive. Evidence: cost-model-2026q4.pdf (in Drive).

If we keep a single score, I recommend 4/5 weighted by customer revenue, not 3/5.

- Laura

Laura Bennett
